I am 63 years old, with only primary school education. I have been farming this land in Quzhou for over 40 years — my father taught me, and I do what has always worked. I have 8 mu of farmland. I don't rent more land anymore; my back and knees can't handle it, and my son works in Shijiazhuang.

I grow winter wheat and summer maize on the same 8 mu, same as everyone in my village. I stopped growing cotton years ago — too much work, and picking it ruins my back. Vegetables are too risky; prices go up and down, and you have to watch them every day. Wheat and maize prices are stable, and the grain dealer comes right to the village.

My wheat is already in the ground — I sowed it last October after hiring the rotary tiller to prepare the soil. I use *luyuan502*, an improved seed I buy from the seed shop. I don't save my own wheat seeds anymore; the yield is poor compared to the bagged seed. At sowing I put about 100 jin of compound fertilizer in the furrow. Now that it is greening up, I will topdress urea and irrigate soon. I irrigate wheat three times: at green-up, at jointing, and at heading. The tube well water is cheap here. I spray insecticide twice when I see aphids, herbicide once, and fungicide once against rust.

After wheat harvest in early June, I immediately plant *denghai605* maize — it is a hybrid seed, and everyone here uses it because it yields well and resists lodging. I plant no-tillage because the window between wheat harvest and maize sowing is short; if I wait for tillage, I might miss the rain. I put compound fertilizer in the seed furrow. Maize needs less water; I irrigate twice, once after sowing if it is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. I spray insecticide twice and herbicide once. Maize does not usually need fungicide here.

I expect about 1000 jin per mu for wheat and 1100 jin per mu for maize. I sell most of it and keep enough flour and cornmeal for my wife and me.
